current.text: Cleveland traded a first-round pick and money to Denver to get Watson.
He is the projected starting forward next to James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.
Experts expect a locked-in starting job at 30 or more minutes, with a solid minutes floor and a more stable role than in Denver.
His usage is expected to fall from 21% to about 19 or 20 next to Mitchell, Harden and Mobley.
He is expected to block fewer shots playing next to Mobley and Allen.
His upside mostly depends on injuries to others. His usage would rise if Harden, Mobley or Mitchell missed games, and his blocks would rise if Allen missed games.

One expert doubts Cleveland paid a first-round pick to use him only as a low-usage corner shooter. He calls Watson his best target on the team and says Watson beats his draft spot if he reaches 23% usage.
He is falling in drafts. Experts call him a safe pick with upside around Yahoo rank 120 and good value at pick 135.
One expert is not convinced his strong three-point shooting from last season is real.
Cleveland may close games with Mobley at center now that Watson is on the team.
Cleveland lost Max Strus, Dennis Schroder, Keon Ellis and Dean Wade. Behind Mobley and Allen there is little frontcourt depth.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With our March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and then 2 games in the fantasy playoff weeks, so finals week has only two games.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games.
Head coach Kenny Atkinson is reported to be under pressure.

durable.text: Blocks are his best category. He blocks a lot of shots for a forward, his steals are okay and he is not a great rebounder.
He is a spot-up three-point shooter, best from the corners. His 3P% has risen every year, from just under 30% to 35% to 41%, and his FT% has also climbed every year.
He is rated a good defender.
He handled higher usage well in Denver when Nikola Jokic and others were out. His usage rose from 21% to 24% with Jokic, Christian Braun and Cam Johnson off the court.
He has only one really good NBA season so far.
A significant hamstring injury ended his 2025-26 season.

note: Watson costs 1 USD on Yahoo and 2 USD on ESPN, with ranks of 125 and 105. That puts him near the end of our 144-player pool, so he is a last-dollar buy with a secure 30-minute starting job. His standout category is blocks (+1.5 z vs the pool, +2.0 vs forwards). A 72% FT% is only a mild drag, so no build has to avoid him, though a two-game finals week in week 21 lowers his playoff value. Early in the season, check whether his usage gets near the 23% that experts say would make him beat his price, and whether he keeps hitting threes at last season's 41%.
